https://punchng.com/fani-kayode-assumes-.summary: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has formally assumed diplomatic duties following the presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence to the South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation. https://punchng.com/fani-kayode-assumes-.body: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has formally assumed diplomatic duties following the presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence to the South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation. Fani-Kayode disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Saturday, announcing that he presented the documents to the department’s Deputy Director-General of Public Diplomacy and Acting Chief of State Protocol, Clayson Monyela, on Friday. According to him, the presentation marked an important diplomatic milestone and the formal commencement of his duties as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, effective October 30. “Following the presentation, I also met with Ambassador Seboga, Deputy Director-General of DIRCO, in his office, as part of my initial diplomatic engagements with senior South African government officials,” he added. Fani-Kayode said the presentation of the copies of the Letters of Credence would precede the ceremonial presentation of the original documents to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. “The presentation of copies of my Letters of Credence precedes the ceremonial presentation of my Letters of Credence to His Excellency, President Cyril Ramaphosa of the Republic of South Africa, which will take place in a few days’ time,” he stated. https://punchng.com/fani-kayode-assumes-.body_zh: 尼日利亚驻南非高级专员费米·法尼-卡约德在向南非国际关系与合作部递交国书副本后，正式开始履行外交职务。法尼-卡约德周六通过其X账号发布消息宣布，他于周五向该部门公共外交副总监兼代理国家礼宾司司长克莱森·莫涅拉递交了相关文件。据他介绍，此次递交标志着重要的外交里程碑，也意味着他自10月30日起正式开始担任尼日利亚驻南非高级专员。他补充道：“递交文件后，我还在办公室会见了南非国际关系与合作部副总监Seboga大使，作为我最初与南非政府高级官员开展外交交涉的一部分。”法尼-卡约德表示，递交国书副本后 数日内将正式向南非总统西里尔·拉马福萨递交国书正本。他指出：“我递交国书副本后，将在几天后的仪式上向南非共和国总统西里尔·拉马福萨阁下正式递交国书正本。”奥卢根贝加·伊格是《Punch》报 journalist，拥有9年以上的专业报道经验。他以敏锐的视角发掘引人入胜的故事，并擅长识别具有新闻价值的发展。多年来，奥卢根贝加凭借将线索转化为清晰、引人入胜且结构严谨的报道，赢得了声誉。他的工作体现了深厚的新闻编辑室经验、编辑判断力，以及对准确、有影响力新闻报道的投入。

https://leadership.ng/breaking-adc-gover.body: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, has raised the alarm over an alleged threat to his life following an attack on his convoy. In a statement by his Media Aide, Aminu Abdullahi, Dan’iya alleged that the attack was carried out by personnel of the Sokoto Marshal and Sokoto State Community Guard Corps. He said the incident reportedly occurred at about 9pm on Friday at the Sokoto Airport area after he escorted Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal to the airport for his return journey to Abuja following political engagements in the state. Dan’iya described the incident as a dangerous escalation of political hostility and an unacceptable threat to democratic participation, while noting that personnel of the two state security outfits blocked his convoy and refused to allow it to pass, claiming they were acting on orders from above not to allow ADC members into Sokoto. According to him, efforts by his security team to resolve the confrontation failed, gunshots were fired, his vehicle was smashed, and two Department of State Services (DSS) officers attached to his team were detained. Dan’iya said he escaped but regarded the actions as a direct threat to his safety. The ADC candidate said earlier on Friday that he and his team observed an increased presence of Sokoto Marshal and Community Guard personnel at entry points into the state, where vehicles bearing ADC inscriptions were allegedly being stopped from entering. He said the convoy initially understood the deployments to be routine security measures but now feared they might be part of a deliberate attempt to restrict ADC activities and endanger its leadership. “If security personnel can block a gubernatorial candidate, fire gunshots during a confrontation, damage his vehicle and detain officers assigned to his protection, then the people of Sokoto deserve urgent answers. No one should be above the law, and no security outfit should be used to threaten political opponents,” Dan’iya said. He said he had reported the incident to the Commissioner of Police in Sokoto. Dan’iya called on the Commissioner of Police, the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the DSS, and other relevant authorities to investigate the incident immediately, determine who issued the orders, identify those responsible for any unlawful conduct, and ensure the prompt release of the two detained DSS officers. He also demanded that evidence, including available footage, operational records, witness accounts and firearm reports, be preserved and examined. The ADC candidate called on the Federal Government, the National Assembly, human rights institutions and the international community to pay urgent attention to the situation and support the protection of democratic freedoms. He urged the Sokoto State Government to clarify the alleged instructions attributed to the security personnel and ensure that state security outfits operate within the law and remain politically neutral. “Sokoto is not the property of any government or political party. Every Nigerian has the right to enter the state, move freely and participate in lawful political activities. Any order intended to exclude ADC members from Sokoto would be unacceptable and must be investigated,” he said. Dan’iya said intimidation or violence would not force him or the ADC to abandon lawful political activities. When called for confirmation, PPRO Sokoto State Police Command DSP Ahmed Rufai didn’t pick up his calls. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/breaking-adc-gover.body_zh: 索科托州非洲民主党（ADC）州长候选人曼尼尔·穆罕默德·丹亚先生就其车队遭袭后 allegedly 有人威胁其生命一事发出警报。丹亚的媒体助手阿米努·阿卜杜拉希发表声明称，丹亚指控袭击是由索科托法警和索科托州社区卫队人员实施的。他说，据报道，事件发生于星期五晚上9时左右，地点在索科托机场一带；此前，他护送参议员阿米努·瓦齐里·坦布瓦尔前往机场，后者结束在该州的政治活动后返回阿布贾。丹亚称，这起事件是政治敌对行为危险升级的表现，也是对参与民主活动的不可接受威胁。他指出，州内两支安全机构的人员拦截了他的车队，拒不让人通行，并声称奉命行事，不允许ADC成员进入索科托。据他称，其安保团队为化解对峙所作的努力未能成功，期间有人开枪，他的车辆遭砸，随行团队中的两名国家情报与安全局（DSS）人员被拘留。丹亚表示，他成功脱身，但认为相关行为直接威胁到他的安全。这位ADC候选人此前在星期五表示，他与团队发现，索科托法警和社区卫队人员在各州界入口的部署有所增加，悬挂ADC标识的车辆据称遭到拦截，无法进入该州。他说，车队起初以为这些部署属于例行安保措施，但如今担心这可能是旨在限制ADC活动并危及该党领导层的蓄意行动。丹亚说：“如果安保人员能够拦截州长候选人，在对峙期间开枪，损坏其车辆，并拘留负责保护他的官员，那么索科托人民理应尽快得到答案。任何人都不应凌驾于法律之上，也不应利用任何安全机构威胁政治对手。”他说，他已向索科托警察局长报告此事。丹亚要求索科托警察局长、警察总监察长、DSS总局长及其他相关当局立即调查事件，查明命令由谁下达，找出任何违法行为责任人，并确保两名被拘留的DSS人员立即获释。他还要求保存并审查证据，包括现有录像、行动记录、证人陈述和枪械报告。这位ADC候选人呼吁联邦政府、国民议会、人权机构及国际社会紧急关注局势，并支持保护民主自由。他敦促索科托州政府澄清据称向安全人员下达的指令，并确保州内安全机构依法行事，保持政治中立。丹亚说：“索科托不是任何政府或政党的财产。每一名尼日利亚公民都有权进入该州、自由通行并参与合法政治活动。任何意图将ADC成员排除在索科托之外的命令都不可接受，必须接受调查。”丹亚表示，恐吓或暴力不会迫使他或ADC放弃合法政治活动。经致电核实，索科托州警察司令部公共关系官 DSP 艾哈迈德·鲁法伊未接听电话。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角将直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过 WhatsApp 获取全天候最新消息 →

Electricity prices in the Philippines keep skyrocketing for all sorts of reasons beyond the control of ordinary Filipino consumers. Volatile price changes have led to a surge in demand for solar installation , with the Philippines becoming the largest market for solar panels after the Netherlands in 2026. It’s clear that more and more Filipinos are recognizing that rooftop solar is the path forward for anyone who fears mounting electricity bills and frequent power outages. But the main question for anyone considering switching to solar is this: Can an ordinary Filipino household really afford it? Solar panel prices have been falling dramatically over the past 15 years, making it the world’s “ cheapest electricity in history ” since 2020, according to the International Energy Agency. In the Philippines, estimates for how much a full solar setup can cost differ depending on the energy capacity, equipment used, and where the equipment is sourced. One such estimate from Let’s Go Renewable , a Philippine advocacy platform campaign for more affordable solar energy, said that a basic solar system for a typical Filipino household may range from P80,000 to P200,000, while larger systems for bigger homes can exceed P500,000. Aside from lower prices, financing options have come a long way in the last year when it comes to easing the burden on a Filipino household’s monthly expenses. But for Philline Donggay, project lead for the Mindanao Goes Solar movement, the country’s roster of existing options still has a long way to go before we can say that solar financing in the Philippines is truly accessible. According to her, options for residential solar financing in Mindanao and other provinces outside the Greater Manila Area remain limited, while the currently available options from government financing institutions are subject to extremely tedious processes and requirements. Confused about how to navigate all the new possibilities — and remaining constraints — in getting a rooftop solar setup? Here’s what you need to know about the current solar financing landscape and where it may be headed. Financing for solar installations most often come in the form of loans. The most common and accessible of these are from government bodies. The GSIS and SSS loans were announced just this year, in the wake of the Middle East oil crisis and the solar boom that ensued in the Philippines. Some commercial and rural banks have since followed suit with solar loan options of their own. For households that cannot put up collateral or have other difficulties meeting the requirements of these institutions, Donggay and Dimalanta said that some solar installers also provide an option called in-house financing. Compared to loans from financial institutions, however, this option usually has a shorter time period — therefore, higher monthly payments — and a higher interest rate. Some installers also offer lease or lease-to-own arrangements. While Donggay said a wide array of financing options is always welcome, she still strongly advises households to be the full owner of their own solar setups. “To me, the promise of solar goes beyond just getting clean electricity; it’s also being able to be a prosumer — a producer and consumer of clean electricity,” she said. For both Donggay and Dimalanta, a rooftop solar setup is worth it regardless of your household’s current income level or electricity consumption. To them, there is no better time than now to start going solar. According to Donggay, going solar should be a consideration for anyone who feels the burden of rising electricity rates. She said if a household can save for a vacation, they may as well consider using that amount to invest in solar technology. Savings from that investment will add up in the long run, after all. “We need to look at how much of a household’s income goes toward paying for their electricity bill,” she said. “Most of the time, we want to consider these options (rooftop solar) because we want to keep more of our income for our other needs.” In the end, it’s a question of where you want your household’s monthly income to go. Staying connected to a traditional distribution utility means endlessly paying a monthly electric bill, with no control over whether those services improve, deteriorate, or get more expensive. With solar financing options, your endless electricity bills may be replaced with finite monthly amortizations. And because rooftop solar setups have an estimated lifespan of 20 to 25 years, you would basically be free from monthly payments after the loan period is over. There are other ways to make your solar setup more affordable. Dimalanta shared two tips. First, she said installing batteries right away is not really a necessity — especially since these components are usually the most expensive part of a rooftop solar setup. “If you are, for example, in the Meralco franchise area or in a franchise area where the distribution utility is relatively reliable — and blackouts don’t frequently happen — maybe you don’t need the battery yet,” she said. Instead, she advises consumers to ask their installer to set up a battery-ready system. Since battery prices are expected to go down as the technology develops, consumers can buy them later to get even more savings out of their solar system. Her second tip is for households to apply for net-metering, which is a program that allows qualified consumers with renewable energy systems to sell the excess power they generate in exchange for credits on their electricity bills. This means that if there are months in the year or times in the day when no one is home or electricity consumption is low, electricity generated during that time could be sold. As a result, the cost recovery on a household’s solar system becomes faster. “So, a project that would have been projected to take 10 years before you got a return on investment may instead take only five years,” she said. While solar financing options have come a long way since rooftop solar technologies were first pushed in the country a decade ago , Donggay said the reality is that existing options remain limited — especially outside highly urbanized areas. That’s not the only way rural areas are disadvantaged when it comes to getting value for their solar setups. Net-metering is a big draw for many prospective solar buyers, but the reality is that off-grid and geographically isolated areas simply do not have that option available. “But even without net-metering, solar installations can still be worthwhile and can be beneficial to households located in off-grid areas for energy security,” she said. “And then you manage your costs, because [almost all of the power] supply to our off-grid areas comes from diesel plants. And that’s why — while diesel costs continue to increase — your bills will also continue to increase,” she said. But beyond all that, the fact remains that there are communities where individual solar home systems are still considered too expensive even with the current financing options. Dimalanta acknowledged this. “And my answer to that is: then let’s make it available to ordinary Filipinos,” she said. For both Dimalanta and Donggay, one of the key solutions lies in our communities — especially in community solar projects where residents only use the power for their own consumption, without needing to sell it. “For example, if this entire barangay or this sitio cannot afford individual solar home systems, is there idle land there or is there a rooftop in all these multipurpose halls that will be built?” she said. “Can they host solar facilities that can supply the immediate vicinity [with power]?” Donggay’s own suggestion is similar: rooftop solar being pre-installed in government housing projects for the urban poor. “We need to be more creative in how we incorporate solar in other projects that are addressing rural and urban development — especially for the people we know would never be approved for a loan by commercial banks,” she added. Solar may be relatively more affordable now than a decade ago, but there’s still a long way to go to make it truly accessible to the households that need it the most. “The answer shouldn’t be: let’s set aside or dismiss solar because it’s only for the rich,” Dimalanta said. “No. I think it poses a real challenge for all of us — government of course included — to make solar affordable to all.” – Rappler.com Upgrade to Rappler+ for exclusive content and unlimited access

https://leadership.ng/masussukas-murder-.body: Masussuka , who was killed with his friend, Adamu Abubakar, by motorcycle-riding gunmen outside his residence in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, just hours before a major national peace gathering, was noted for his progressive work in promoting inter-communal unity, peace-building, and theological moderation. Within the heterogeneous Islamic landscape in Nigeria and West Africa, Sheikh Masussuka was not only a distinct cleric; some saw him as a polarising preacher who practised the ‘Tafseerul Qur’ani bil Qur’an’ method. Some recognise this form of Islamic scholarship as the most authoritative and purest methodology of Tafsir (exegesis), anchored in using only the holy book for sermons and not relying primarily on outside sources. Masussuka’s reliance on the Holy Qur’an for interpretation led him to reject or strongly criticise certain Hadith traditions. His preaching style regularly put him in theological conflict with groups opposed to his approach. The Ansaru – an Al-Qaeda affiliate operating in West Africa- claimed responsibility for the murder, labelling the 47-year-old Islamic cleric an ‘infidel’. With the group claiming responsibility for his killing, intra-faith conflict served as a major cause for his murder. Beyond internal doctrinal debates, the cleric stood as nationally and globally recognised as a tireless champion of religious harmony. He was not only decorated as a Peace Ambassador by the Network for Good Governance and Transparency in 2025, but also used his media channels, including his dedicated Qur’an TV and Radio stations, to de-radicalise youths and advocate for friendly, peaceful coexistence between Nigeria’s Muslim and Christian populations. Masussuka’s killing has introduced frightening uncertainty and leaves behind multi-layered consequences for interfaith relations and religious freedom. His murder has left a yawning hole of threat for the survival of moderate voices in the North, which is facing the peril of religious conflagration. With Masussuka’s death, one of the strongest bridges for both Nigeria’s intra-faith and inter-faith relations has been destroyed. Above all, the cleric recognised the need for intra-faith work, and he worked assiduously to tackle issues that threaten peaceful coexistence among sects within Islam. The murder of the Sheikh by the Ansaru group clearly points to a dilemma facing intra-faith work. Within fractured societies bedevilled by violence and bloodshed, peace does not occur organically; clerics like Masussuka build it through deliberate, courageous labour. By establishing schools, the late cleric deployed integrated conventional and Islamic curricula and, using mass media to spread counter-extremism messages, supplied a platform to de-radicalise youths from the dangers of extremist positions. The killing of the Katsina State-born cleric is a big loss to current efforts in realising peaceful coexistence in Nigeria, especially in the North. It is troubling that when rogue politicians weaponise religion for political relevance, the death of Masussuka amounts to a yawning hole in the dream of rallying both Muslims and Christians in achieving the common objectives in standing up for peace. It is a kind of paradox that the cleric, who cherished peace and was famous for preaching unity among Muslims and non-Muslims, had his life terminated by violent men. The life of Masussuka epitomises the courage to stand up for one’s belief, no matter the threats. He knew the implications of defending what he believed and never shrank from doing what he felt was in the best interest of not only Islam but humanity. The death of this prominent voice may create an immediate vacuum, but those whose lives were touched by Masussuka may take up his mantle of leadership, committed to broadening the space for interfaith engagement and never leaving vulnerable communities exposed to polarised rhetoric. The assassination of Masussuka has thrown a cloud of uncertainty over the religious intelligentsia striving to retrieve people from polarising sermons that preach hatred and death to those outside of their fold. Masussuka joins other prominent clerics murdered over the last two decades by terror groups for refusing to bow to violent extremism. We must never allow the killing of clerics for being moderates and promoting religious freedom. The killings and intimidation of moderate scholars who might otherwise speak out against hate speech or participate in cross-religious alliances may lead them to choose self-censorship to protect their families. Allowing moderate voices to fall silent out of fear will automatically mean that the narrative space is completely conceded to violent extremists, therefore making prospects for sustainable interfaith peace increasingly unattainable. Following the killing of the cleric, the Katsina State Governor, Dr Dikko Umaru Radda, has condemned the attack and applauded Sheikh Masussuka’s devotion to peace. With Ansaru claiming responsibility for the murder, the government should focus on encouraging the emergence of more Sheikhs who will follow in the footsteps of Masussuka to realise the structural reform the cleric paid the supreme price for. To avoid future killings of moderate voices, the government must become an active protector, instead of a tireless mourner. Clerics engaged in de-radicalisation and interfaith work should not be left to the whims and caprices of terror groups. Now that arrangements have been concluded to pass legislation on State Police, governors of the North must step up to the occasion and protect high-risk peace-builders from enemies of peace. Masussuka’s death has brought home the lesson that the protection of intra-faith and inter-faith workers must never be relegated but must be considered a core national security imperative. The most fitting tribute to Masussuka’s legacy must be one anchored on Christian and Muslim leaders’ resolve not to bow to terror groups. Nigerians can only honour the Sheikh’s ultimate sacrifice by refusing to cave in to terrorism. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/masussukas-murder-.body_zh: 马苏苏卡与朋友阿达穆·阿布巴卡尔在卡特琳娜州杜钦马住所门外，被骑摩托车的枪手杀害。就在全国性大型和平集会前几个小时遇害的马苏苏卡，以推动族群间团结、和平建设及神学温和化方面的工作而广受关注。在尼日利亚和西非多元复杂的伊斯兰教格局中，谢赫·马苏苏卡不仅是一位颇具特色的宗教人士，有些人还认为他是一位两极分化的布道者，奉行“Tafseerul Qur'ani bil Qur'an”方法。一些人认为，这种伊斯兰学术形式是最具权威性和最纯粹的Tafsir（注释）方法，其核心是仅依据圣书布道，而不主要依赖外部来源。马苏苏卡依靠《古兰经》进行阐释，因而拒绝或严厉批评某些圣训传统。他的布道风格经常使他与反对其主张的团体发生神学冲突。在西非活动的基地组织分支机构Ansaru宣称对这起谋杀负责，并称这位47岁的伊斯兰宗教人士为“异教徒”。该组织宣称对杀害他负责，说明信仰内部冲突是他遇害的重要原因之一。除了内部教义争论之外，这位宗教人士在全国和全球范围内都被公认为不知疲倦地倡导宗教和谐的人士。他不仅在2025年被治理与透明度网络授予和平大使称号，还利用自己的媒体平台，包括专门设立的《古兰经》电视台和广播电台，推动青年去极端化，并倡导尼日利亚穆斯林与基督徒友好、和平共处。马苏苏卡遇害带来了令人不安的不确定性，并对宗教间关系和宗教自由造成多层面后果。他的遇害使北方温和派声音的生存面临巨大威胁和缺口，而该地区正处在宗教冲突的危险之中。随着马苏苏卡去世，尼日利亚信仰内部和宗教之间关系中最有力的一座桥梁之一被摧毁。尤为重要的是，这位宗教人士认识到开展信仰内部工作的必要性，并不懈努力处理威胁伊斯兰教内部各派和平共处的问题。Ansaru杀害这位谢赫，显然凸显了信仰内部工作面临的两难。在饱受暴力和血腥冲突困扰的分裂社会中，和平不会自发实现；像马苏苏卡这样的宗教人士通过有意识且勇敢的努力来建设和平。已故宗教人士创办学校，将常规课程与伊斯兰课程融为一体，并借助大众媒体传播反极端主义信息，为青年摆脱极端主义立场的危险提供了平台。杀害这位出生于卡特琳娜州的宗教人士，对当前实现尼日利亚和平共处，尤其是北方地区的和平共处，是一项重大损失。令人不安的是，当不择手段的政治人物把宗教作为谋取政治影响力的工具时，马苏苏卡的死亡就为团结穆斯林和基督徒、争取共同目标并捍卫和平的梦想留下了一个巨大缺口。这是一种悖论：这位珍视和平、并因倡导穆斯林与非穆斯林团结而闻名的宗教人士，却被暴力分子夺去了生命。马苏苏卡的一生体现了无论面对何种威胁，都要坚持自身信仰的勇气。他清楚捍卫信念可能带来的后果，却从不退缩，始终去做他认为不仅符合伊斯兰教利益、也符合全人类利益的事情。这位杰出声音的逝去可能立即造成真空，但那些生命受到马苏苏卡影响的人可能接过他的领导重任，致力于扩大宗教间互动的空间，并避免让脆弱社群暴露在两极化言论之中。马苏苏卡遇刺使宗教知识界笼罩在不确定的阴霾之下；这个群体正努力把人们从宣扬仇恨与死亡的偏极布道中拯救出来。过去20年间，马苏苏卡与其他多位杰出宗教人士一样，因拒绝屈从于暴力极端主义而被恐怖组织杀害。我们绝不能允许宗教人士仅仅因为立场温和并推动宗教自由而遭到杀害。对那些本可挺身反对仇恨言论或参与跨宗教联盟的温和派学者的杀戮和恐吓，可能迫使他们选择自我审查，以保护家人。若任由温和派因恐惧而噤声，就等于自动把叙事空间完全拱手让给暴力极端分子，从而使实现可持续宗教间和平的前景愈发遥不可及。宗教人士遇害后，卡特琳娜州州长Dikko Umaru Radda博士谴责了这次袭击，并赞扬谢赫·马苏苏卡对和平的奉献。Ansaru宣称对这起谋杀负责，政府应着重鼓励更多谢赫循马苏苏卡的足迹前行，以实现这位宗教人士付出最高代价所追求的结构性改革。为避免温和派人士今后再次遇害，政府必须成为积极的保护者，而不是 endlessly哀悼的送葬者。参与去极端化和宗教间工作的宗教人士，不应任由恐怖集团随意摆布。如今，关于推动州警察立法的安排已经敲定，北方各州州长必须挺身而出，保护高风险的和平建设者，使其免受和平敌人的伤害。马苏苏卡之死再次带回一个教训：保护信仰内部和宗教间工作者绝不能被降为次要事项，而必须被视为核心的国家安全 imperative。纪念马苏苏卡精神遗产的最佳方式，就是以基督徒和穆斯林领袖坚定不移地拒绝向恐怖组织屈服为根基。尼日利亚人只有拒绝向恐怖主义让步，才能不辜负这位谢赫的最终牺牲。请点击进入我们的报道边缘，获取实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp频道，随时随地接收全天候更新 →

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/debt.summary: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/debt.summary_zh: 前总统奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔批评总统博拉·蒂努布为政府借款辩护，称债务比麻风病更可怕，因为它会对当代和子孙后代造成毁灭性后果。针对蒂努布此前关于借款“不是麻风病”的说法，奥巴桑乔认为，公共债务的不断累积可能使国家的未来被抵押，并给尚未出生的世代施加难以承受的负担。债务比麻风病更可怕，因为麻风病只摧毁一个人。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/debt.body: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said. He urged Nigerian leaders to scrutinise foreign economic prescriptions and ensure that national policies reflected the country’s interests and development priorities. Turning to artificial intelligence, Obasanjo warned that Africa risked repeating the mistakes of its colonial past if it allowed foreign interests to control the technology and its applications. Although he acknowledged that he was not technically knowledgeable about AI, he said ownership and control were critical to ensuring that the technology served African interests. “I don’t know too much technically about AI, but I know that anything that is not under your control can be abused against you. And you can see that this has already started,” he said. Drawing parallels between AI and Africa’s historical experiences with slavery, colonialism and economic dependency, Obasanjo urged African leaders to approach the technological revolution with caution. He also questioned the concept of technology transfer, asking African countries to examine the terms and benefits of their engagements with foreign technology providers. “But what exactly is technology transfer? Who transferred technology to them, and what did they pay for it?” he queried. Obasanjo further criticised what he described as unequal international economic arrangements, citing restrictions on agricultural subsidies for developing countries despite continued support for farmers in developed economies. He expressed concern over the estimated 24 million Nigerian children out of school, warning that the situation could create serious challenges for future generations. “We have 24 million Nigerian children who should be in school but are not. If you are looking for the disasters of tomorrow, these children represent one of them,” he said. He challenged policymakers and technology stakeholders to explore how AI could improve access to education and address learning challenges. On agriculture, Obasanjo advocated the deployment of artificial intelligence to help farmers identify suitable crops, improve productivity and strengthen food and nutrition security. Also speaking at the event, guest speaker and historian, Dr Umar Ardo, warned that Africa could be entering another phase of economic exploitation through artificial intelligence if it failed to secure ownership and control of its data, technological infrastructure and intellectual resources. In a presentation titled, “From Slave Ships to Server Farms: Artificial Intelligence and Africa’s Unbroken History of Extraction”, Ardo argued that although AI offered significant opportunities for economic transformation, it could deepen existing inequalities if African countries remained dependent on foreign technology companies. He said the continent must move beyond adopting foreign innovations and address fundamental questions surrounding ownership, control, regulation and the distribution of economic benefits. “AI offers Africa important opportunities, but without ownership, safeguards and public purpose, it could extend a long history in which Africa supplies value while others control and capture it,” he said. Tracing Africa’s economic history over five centuries, Ardo identified the transatlantic slave trade, colonial exploitation of natural resources and post-independence economic dependency as major phases of external extraction. He explained that while the slave trade commodified African lives, colonialism focused largely on exploiting mineral and agricultural resources, while many post-independence economies remained dependent on exporting raw materials and importing finished products. According to him, infrastructure and technologies introduced during colonial rule, including railways, steam engines and administrative systems, were largely organised around extracting African resources and transporting them to foreign markets. “We supplied resources and labour; others controlled the machinery and captured much of the value,” he stated. Ardo also identified the migration of highly trained African professionals, including doctors, nurses, engineers and scientists, to foreign countries as another dimension of the continent’s continuing resource losses. He warned that data could become the next major commodity in Africa’s history of external extraction, noting that information generated by citizens, hospitals, farmers, businesses, indigenous communities and public institutions was increasingly valuable to the global digital economy. “Data may become the fourth commodity in this long history of extraction,” he cautioned. The historian expressed concern that the infrastructure for processing information, developing AI models and generating intellectual property and commercial profits remained disproportionately controlled outside Africa. He questioned who benefited when farmers’ agricultural practices, patients’ medical records, indigenous languages, traditional medicine and cultural knowledge were incorporated into AI systems developed by foreign companies. “When farmers’ planting patterns are recorded, who controls that knowledge; the farmer or the platform?” he asked. To prevent artificial intelligence from becoming another instrument of economic dependency, Ardo proposed a framework anchored on technological sovereignty, data protection, indigenous innovation, grassroots development and continental cooperation. He called for stronger legal and institutional safeguards against the uncontrolled exploitation of personal data and traditional knowledge. While acknowledging the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 as an important step towards protecting citizens’ information, he said privacy protection alone was insufficient to guarantee data sovereignty. He advocated additional mechanisms to protect community knowledge, ensure fair compensation and guarantee Africans a reasonable share of the commercial value generated from their data and intellectual resources. Ardo urged the Federal Government to increase investment in domestic computing capacity, reliable energy infrastructure, semiconductor technology, research institutions and indigenous AI development. He maintained that Nigeria, with a population exceeding 230 million, should not remain merely a consumer market for foreign technology. “A country of over 230 million people should be more than a market for foreign technology,” he declared. He also called for the development of locally controlled datasets and AI models capable of understanding African languages, agricultural practices, medicinal traditions and customary knowledge under African ownership and appropriate safeguards. On grassroots development, Ardo urged governments to ensure that communities benefited directly from AI applications in primary healthcare, agricultural extension services, local government administration, revenue collection, conflict resolution and disaster management. He further advocated comprehensive AI training programmes in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to develop software developers, technicians, data stewards and other professionals. On continental cooperation, he urged Nigeria to work with other African countries to harmonise data governance regulations, develop shared technological infrastructure and strengthen the continent’s bargaining power in engagements with international technology companies. He identified the African Union’s Data Policy Framework, adopted in 2022, as an important foundation for coordinated continental action. Warning that digital extraction could be more difficult to identify and resist than the exploitation of physical resources, Ardo said information could cross national borders without the knowledge or meaningful understanding of the people and communities generating it. “One of the most efficient systems of extraction is the one its subjects volunteer to use,” he warned. He urged African leaders to approach the AI revolution with a clear understanding of the continent’s history, insisting that Africa must become a builder, owner and rule-maker in the global technology ecosystem rather than remain a passive consumer of foreign innovations. Drawing a comparison between Africa’s historical experiences and the emerging digital economy, he said: “Five centuries ago, they came for our bodies. Then they came for our land and its riches. Then our commodities and trained minds. Today, they come for our data.” He, however, maintained that Africa still had the opportunity to determine its technological future. “The choice is ours. Artificial intelligence can become another instrument through which Africa is managed, or an instrument through which Africa begins to manage its own destiny,” he added. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/debt.body_zh: 前总统奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔批评总统博拉·蒂努布为政府借款辩护，称债务比麻风病更可怕，因为它会给当代和子孙后代带来毁灭性后果。奥巴桑乔还警告尼日利亚和其他非洲国家，不要让外国利益集团主导人工智能（AI），并指出，如果非洲大陆未能发展自身的技术能力，这项新兴技术可能成为又一种剥削工具和数字殖民主义工具。前总统于周五在奥贡州阿贝奥库塔举行的Ajibosin Platform公共论坛上发言，本次论坛的主题是“利用人工智能解决基层问题并推动国家发展”。针对蒂努布此前关于“借款不是麻风病”的说法，奥巴桑乔认为，公共债务不断累积可能抵押国家的未来，并给尚未出生的世代带来难以承受的重担。他说：“任何人说债务不是麻风病，都完全是胡扯。债务比麻风病更可怕，因为麻风病只摧毁一个人，债务却摧毁几代人。”今年4月，蒂努布曾为其政府的借款政策辩护，坚持认为，只要国家有能力偿还，借款本身并非错误。总统在州政府与高原州领导人的会议上说：“如果我们必须借款，我们就借。借款不是麻风病；我们只需努力工作，确保有能力偿还。”出席会议的包括州长Caleb Mutfwang和全进步大会全国主席Nentawe Yilwatda教授。总统的立场正值外界对尼日利亚债务规模日益上升、政府收入中用于偿债的比例不断提高感到担忧之际。奥巴桑乔还质疑尼日利亚多年来的经济表现，尤其是奈拉对美元贬值的问题。他回忆自己作为农民的经历说，47年前创办农场时，奈拉比美元强势。他问道：“47年前我开始经营农场时，1奈拉可以兑换1.85美元。47年前。尼日利亚在这47年里做了什么，竟让我们如今要用1,500奈拉兑换1美元？我们做了什么？”他向国家政治领导层提出挑战，要求其展现对尼日利亚问题的了解，并找出应对国家所面临挑战的实际解决办法。他追问：“我们的领导人知道什么？他们又不知道什么？根据他们所知道的，他们能为我们做什么？”前总统还指责尼日利亚依赖世界银行和国际货币基金组织（IMF），认为这些机构提出的经济处方未必是为解决该国特殊国情而设计的。他说：“世界银行和IMF不是为我们而设计的。它们不是由我们建立的。它们在我们独立之前就已建成，而决定我们将做什么的，正是这些人。”他敦促尼日利亚领导人审视外国经济处方，确保国家政策反映国家利益和发展重点。谈到人工智能时，奥巴桑乔警告，如果非洲允许外国利益集团控制这项技术及其应用，非洲就有重蹈殖民历史覆辙的风险。尽管他承认自己在AI技术方面并不专业，但他说，所有权和控制权对于确保技术服务于非洲利益至关重要。他说：“我在AI技术方面了解得不算多，但我知道，任何不受你控制的东西，都可能被用来伤害你。你可以看到，这种情况已经开始。”奥巴桑乔将AI与非洲在奴隶制、殖民主义和经济依赖方面的历史经历相提并论，敦促非洲领导人谨慎应对这场技术革命。他还质疑技术转让的概念，要求非洲国家审视与外国技术提供方合作时的条款和收益。他问道：“技术转让究竟是什么？是谁把技术转让给他们的？他们为此支付了什么？”奥巴桑乔进一步批评他所称的不平等国际经济安排，并指出，发展中国家农业补贴受到限制之际，发达经济体却继续向农民提供支持。他对估计有2,400万尼日利亚儿童失学表示担忧，警告这种状况可能给未来世代造成严重挑战。他说：“我们有2,400万尼日利亚儿童本应在校学习，却未能入学。如果你在寻找明天的灾难，这些儿童就是灾难之一。”他向政策制定者和技术界人士提出挑战，要求探索如何利用AI改善教育可及性并解决学习难题。在农业方面，奥巴桑乔主张部署人工智能，帮助农民识别适宜种植的作物、提高生产率，并加强粮食和营养安全。也在此次活动上发言的客座演讲者、历史学家Umar Ardo博士警告，如果非洲未能确保拥有并控制自己的数据、技术基础设施和智力资源，非洲可能正通过人工智能进入另一个经济剥削阶段。在题为“从奴隶船到服务器农场：人工智能与非洲从未中断的掠夺史”的演示中，Ardo认为，尽管AI为经济转型提供了重大机会，但如果非洲国家继续依赖外国技术公司，它也可能加剧现有不平等。他说，非洲大陆必须超越单纯采用外国创新品的阶段，并处理围绕所有权、控制权、监管和经济收益分配的根本问题。他说：“AI为非洲提供了重要机会，但如果没有所有权、保障措施和公共目的，它可能延续一段漫长的历史，即非洲提供价值，而他人控制并攫取这些价值。”Ardo追溯了非洲500年的经济历史，将跨大西洋奴隶贸易、殖民时期对自然资源的掠夺以及独立后的经济依赖列为外部资源掠夺的主要阶段。他解释说，奴隶贸易将非洲人的生命商品化，殖民主义主要聚焦于掠夺矿产和农业资源，而许多独立后的经济体仍依赖出口原材料和进口制成品。据他介绍，殖民统治期间引入的铁路、蒸汽机和行政制度等基础设施和技术，很大程度上围绕着掠夺非洲资源并将其运往外国市场而建立。他指出：“我们提供资源和劳动力；他人控制机器，并攫取其中大部分价值。”Ardo还把包括医生、护士、工程师和科学家在内的高素质非洲专业人员迁往外国，视为非洲持续损失资源的另一个方面。他警告，数据可能成为非洲外部掠夺史上的下一大宗商品，并指出，由公民、医院、农民、企业、原住民社区和公共机构产生的信息，对全球数字经济而言正变得愈发 valuable。他提醒说：“数据可能成为这段漫长掠夺史中的第四种商品。”历史学家担忧，用于处理信息、开发AI模型以及创造知识产权和商业利润的基础设施，仍不成比例地由非洲以外控制。他质疑，当农民的农业实践、患者的医疗记录、原住民语言、传统医学和文化知识被纳入外国公司开发的AI系统时，究竟谁才是受益者。他问道：“当农民的种植模式被记录下来时，谁控制这些知识？是农民，还是平台？”为防止人工智能成为又一种经济依赖工具，Ardo提出了一套以技术主权、数据保护、本土创新、基层发展和大陆合作为支柱的框架。他呼吁加强法律和制度保障，防止个人数据和传统知识遭到无控制剥削。他承认《尼日利亚数据保护法（2023年）》是保护公民信息的重要一步，但指出，仅保护隐私不足以保障数据主权。他主张建立额外机制，保护社区知识，确保公平补偿，并保障非洲人获得其数据和智力资源所创造商业价值的合理份额。Ardo敦促联邦政府增加对国内计算能力、可靠能源基础设施、半导体技术、研究机构和本土AI开发的投资。他认为，尼日利亚人口超过2.3亿，不应继续仅仅充当外国技术的消费市场。他宣称：“一个拥有超过2.3亿人口的国家，不应只是外国技术的市场。”他还呼吁开发由非洲拥有并配有适当保障、本地控制的数据集和AI模型，使其能够理解非洲语言、农业实践、医药传统和习惯知识。在基层发展方面，Ardo敦促各国政府确保社区直接受益于AI在初级医疗、农业推广服务、地方政府管理、税收征管、冲突解决和灾害管理中的应用。他还主张在大学、理工学院和教育学院全面开展AI培训项目，培养软件开发者、技术人员、数据管理员及其他专业人士。在大陆合作方面，他敦促尼日利亚与其他非洲国家合作，协调数据治理法规，建设共享技术基础设施，并增强非洲大陆在与国际技术公司交涉时的议价能力。他指出，非洲联盟于2022年通过的《数据政策框架》是协调大陆行动的重要基础。Ardo警告，数字资源掠夺可能比实体资源剥削更难识别和抵制，信息还可能在生成它的人民和社区毫不知情或无法真正理解的情况下跨越国界。他警告说：“最高效的掠夺体系之一，就是其对象自愿使用的体系。”他敦促非洲领导人清醒认识这段大陆历史后应对AI革命，并坚持非洲必须成为全球技术生态中的建设者、所有者 和规则制定者，而不是继续做外国创新品的被动消费者。他在对比非洲历史经历与新兴数字经济时说：“500年前，他们来掠夺我们的身体。然后他们来掠夺我们的土地和财富。接着是我们的商品和训练有素的头脑。今天，他们来掠夺我们的数据。”不过，他仍认为非洲依然有机会决定自己的技术未来。他补充道：“选择权在我们手中。人工智能可能成为非洲再次受人支配的工具，也可能成为非洲开始掌握自身命运的工具。”此处表达的意见不代表Vanguard报纸及其任何员工的观点

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: The federal government has commenced a monthly cash relief programme, offering N50,000 to vulnerable households to cushion the effects of rising living costs. Mr Doro said the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is a presidential initiative aimed at providing immediate financial support to millions of vulnerable Nigerians.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 联邦政府已启动每月现金纾困计划，向困难家庭提供 N50,000，以缓冲生活成本上涨带来的影响。多罗先生表示，全国紧急救援与稳定干预计划（NERSI）是总统发起的一项行动，旨在为数百万处境困难的尼日利亚人提供即时财政支持。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: The federal government has commenced a monthly cash relief programme, offering N50,000 to vulnerable households to cushion the effects of rising living costs. The Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro, announced this in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja. Mr Doro said the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is a presidential initiative aimed at providing immediate financial support to millions of vulnerable Nigerians. He explained that the intervention was introduced in response to global food inflation and the rising cost of essential goods, which had continued to put pressure on household incomes. “Under this intervention, eligible beneficiaries will receive N50,000 monthly, providing direct assistance to help meet essential needs and ease the burden of living costs,” he said. The minister said the programme would be reviewed periodically to reflect changes in the cost of living, adding that beneficiaries would be notified directly before any adjustments were made. According to him, the ministry is collaborating with licensed digital financial service providers to ensure secure, timely and transparent disbursement of the funds. He explained that beneficiaries would receive text messages from the service providers seeking their consent before payments were made directly into their bank accounts or mobile wallets. Mr Doro emphasised that beneficiaries were not required to submit applications, pay fees or register through agents to access the intervention. He also warned Nigerians against fraudsters, urging them not to disclose their Personal Identification Numbers (PINs) or Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) to anyone. “If you are unsure about any message, or anyone asks you for money, call the official NERSI helpline on 0700-022-2222,” he said. The minister described NERSI as complementary to existing federal government social protection and economic support programmes, noting that it was designed to strengthen household resilience and promote economic stability. He added that the intervention aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to implementing the programme with dignity, transparency and accountability
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府开始每月向脆弱民众发放5万奈拉现金
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 联邦政府启动了一项每月现金救济计划，向困难家庭发放N50,000，以缓解生活成本上涨造成的影响。人道主义事务与减贫部长伯纳德·多罗于周五在阿布贾发表声明，宣布了这一消息。多罗先生表示，全国紧急救济与稳定干预计划（NERSI）是一项总统倡议，旨在为数百万处境困难的尼日利亚人提供即时财政支持。他解释道，推出该干预措施是为了应对全球食品通胀以及 essentials 价格上涨，后者持续对家庭收入造成压力。他说：“在这项干预措施下，符合条件的受益人每月将领取N50,000，直接获得援助，以满足基本生活需要并减轻生活成本负担。”部长表示，该计划将定期评估，以反映生活成本的变化，并补充称，在作出任何调整之前，将直接通知受益人。据他介绍，该部正与持牌数字金融服务商合作，确保资金安全、及时、透明地发放。他解释道，在款项直接转入受益人的银行账户或移动钱包之前，服务商会向其发送短信，征求其同意。多罗先生强调，受助人无需提交申请、支付费用或通过代理登记即可获得这项干预措施。他还警告尼日利亚人提防骗子，敦促他们不要向任何人透露个人识别码（PIN）或银行验证码（BVN）。他说：“如果你对任何消息感到不确定，或者有人向你索要钱财，请拨打NERSI官方求助热线0700-022-2222。”部长表示，NERSI是对现有联邦政府社会保护和经济支持计划的补充，旨在增强家庭韧性并促进经济稳定。他补充说，这项干预措施与博拉·蒂努巴总统的“重燃希望议程”保持一致，并重申该部将以尊严、透明和问责方式落实该计划。

https://dailytrust.com/government-reform.body: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended the federal government’s economic reforms, saying they are designed to create an enabling environment for investment, strengthen businesses and improve the country’s productive capacity. He, however, stressed the need for effective communication of government policies at both federal and state levels to help citizens understand their objectives, implementation and expected benefits. Shettima spoke in Abuja at the Dukes Masterclass on Penetrative Leadership, where he highlighted the importance of effective communication in governance and the digital economy. “The reforms undertaken by this administration, including the fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange market liberalisation, fiscal restructuring and revenue mobilisation, represent important steps towards building a more productive, competitive and resilient economy. “These decisions require courage, but beyond the decisions themselves, they are intended to create an environment in which investments can grow, businesses can plan with greater confidence, public resources can be deployed more effectively, and the productive capacity of our people can be better harnessed,” he said. He said the government must communicate its policies clearly, provide credible evidence of progress and listen to citizens’ experiences to build public confidence in its programmes. In his opening address, Otunba Bimbo Ashiru, speaking on the theme, ‘Penetrative Leadership: Definitive Strategies in Robust Crisis and Reputational Management in an Increasingly Chaotic World Order’, also underscored the importance of effective policy communication by leaders and government officials. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/b.body: Hails Tinubu, army chief, Gov Yusuf over strategic military build-up The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau, has hailed the Nigerian Army for deploying a new battalion and an artillery regiment to Kano State, describing the development as a major boost to efforts to crush banditry and other security threats in the North-west. The new military formations comprise the 24 Battalion, established in Tudun Wada, and the 311 Artillery Regiment, located in Dambatta. Barau said the deployment demonstrated President Bola Tinubu’s determination to confront banditry, terrorism and other forms of violent criminality threatening lives and property across the country. The Deputy Senate President, who spoke through a statement issued yesterday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, also commended the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for what he described as visionary leadership and proactive efforts to reposition the military to address emerging security challenges. He said the establishment of the two formations was a significant step towards strengthening the operational capacity of the Nigerian Army and improving its response to security threats in Kano and neighbouring states. He also praised Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, for his commitment to protecting lives and property, stressing that sustained cooperation between the state government and the military would be critical to ensuring that the newly established formations achieved their operational objectives. According to him, effective collaboration between the federal and state governments, as well as security agencies, remains essential to tackling the security challenges confronting the North-west. The Deputy Senate President further appealed to residents of Tudun Wada, Dambatta and other communities across Kano State to support the military and provide the necessary cooperation to enable the new formations to discharge their responsibilities effectively. He particularly urged traditional rulers, community leaders and residents to strengthen their relationship with security agencies by providing timely and credible intelligence on the activities of criminal groups. Barau warned that the fight against banditry and other forms of criminality could not be left exclusively to the military and other security agencies, insisting that community participation was indispensable to achieving lasting security. “The fight against banditry and other forms of criminality is a collective one. I urge all our traditional leaders, community leaders and residents to cooperate fully with the military, share timely intelligence and support these newly established formations to succeed. “Without community support, our security agencies cannot fully defeat these criminals,” he said. He reaffirmed the commitment of the National Assembly, particularly the Senate, to providing the necessary legislative backing and ensuring adequate funding for the Armed Forces and other security agencies. Barau said the Senate would continue to support measures aimed at strengthening the capacity of security institutions to confront banditry, terrorism and other threats to national security. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/b.title_zh: 巴劳：卡诺将组建新陆军营和炮兵团，打击匪盗活动
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/b.body_zh:
巴拉克赞扬提努布、陆军参谋长和州长优素福加强战略军事部署

参议院副议长吉布林·巴劳参议员赞扬尼日利亚陆军向卡诺州部署了一个新营和一个炮兵团，称这一部署将大力支持打击匪盗活动及其他安全威胁的努力，从而改善西北部的安全局势。

新编成的军事单位包括驻扎在图敦瓦达的第24营，以及位于丹巴塔的第311炮兵团。巴劳说，这次部署表明总统博拉·提努布决心打击匪盗活动、恐怖主义及其他威胁全国民众生命和财产的暴力犯罪。

参议院副议长通过其媒体与公共关系特别顾问伊斯梅尔·穆达希尔昨日发表的声明表达上述看法。他还赞扬陆军参谋长瓦伊迪·沙伊布中将，称其展现出富有远见的领导力，并积极推动军队调整部署，以应对不断出现的安全挑战。

他说，组建这两个单位是加强尼日利亚陆军作战能力的重要一步，将提升军队应对卡诺州及邻近各州安全威胁的反应能力。

他还赞扬卡诺州州长阿巴·卡比尔·优素福为保护生命和财产所作的投入，强调州政府与军队持续合作，对于确保新编单位实现作战目标至关重要。

据他介绍，联邦政府、州政府以及安全机构之间的有效协作，仍是解决西北部面临的安全挑战所必需的。

参议院副议长还呼吁图敦瓦达、丹巴塔及卡诺州其他社区的居民支持军队，并给予必要合作，使新编单位能够有效履行职责。

他特别敦促传统 rulers、社区领袖和居民加强与安全机构的联系，及时提供有关犯罪团伙活动的可靠情报。

巴劳警告，打击匪盗活动及其他犯罪不能完全交由军队和其他安全机构负责，而社区参与是实现长久安全不可或缺的条件。

“打击匪盗活动及其他犯罪是全社会的共同责任。我呼吁所有传统 rulers、社区领袖和居民与军队充分合作，及时共享情报，并支持这些新编单位取得成功。‘没有社区的支持，我们的安全机构就无法彻底击败这些犯罪分子。’他说。

他重申国民议会，尤其是参议院，将为武装部队和其他安全机构提供必要的立法支持，并确保获得充足资金。

巴劳表示，参议院将继续支持旨在增强安全机构能力的措施，以打击匪盗活动、恐怖主义及其他危害国家安全的威胁。

https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.summary: The Yobe State Council of the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to the state government to address three key welfare demands or risk industrial action. The ultimatum, which took effect on October 28, 2026, expires at midnight on November 11.
https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.summary_zh: 约贝州教育及相关机构非学术人员工会（NASU）州委员会已向州政府发出最后通牒，要求其在14天内处理三项关键的福利诉求，否则将面临工业行动。最后通牒于2026年10月28日生效，将于11月11日午夜到期。
https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.body: The Yobe State Council of the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to the state government to address three key welfare demands or risk industrial action. The ultimatum, which took effect on October 28, 2026, expires at midnight on November 11. The union’s position was contained in a statement signed by its state chairman, Comrade Ali Usman. Among its demands is the implementation of the 65-year retirement age for non-academic staff in state-owned tertiary institutions. The union is also demanding the immediate implementation of the reviewed 2024 salary table under the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Salary Structure (CONTEDISS), as well as the approval and implementation of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA) and applicable Earned Allowance (EA). While acknowledging the contributions of lecturers to the development of tertiary institutions, the union said non-academic staff also played critical roles in the administrative, technical and operational activities necessary for the effective running of the institutions. It argued that the failure to give non-academic staff equal consideration could undermine institutional efficiency and harmonious industrial relations. The statement added that the prolonged delay in addressing the demands had generated widespread dissatisfaction among members and negatively affected staff morale across the affected institutions. The union urged the state government to use the 14-day ultimatum to take concrete steps towards resolving the issues, warning that failure to meet the demands by November 11 would prompt its leadership to reconvene on November 12 to determine the next line of action in accordance with labour laws. It appealed to Governor Mai Mala Buni and other relevant government stakeholders to intervene and address the demands to avert industrial unrest and possible disruption of academic and administrative activities in the state’s tertiary institutions. https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.title_zh: 尼日利亚全国高校教师工会就福利问题向约贝州政府发出最后通牒
https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.body_zh: 约贝州教育及相关机构非学术人员工会（NASU）州委员会已向州政府发出为期14天的最后通牒，要求解决三项关键福利诉求，否则将面临罢工。这项最后通牒于2026年10月28日生效，将于11月11日午夜到期。工会的立场载于由州主席阿里·乌斯曼同志签署的一份声明中。其诉求包括，在州属高等教育机构落实非学术人员65岁退休年龄。工会还要求立即落实《高等教育机构统一工资结构》（CONTEDISS）下修订后的2024年工资表，并批准和落实《统一非教学工具津贴》（CONTTA）以及适用的 earned allowance（EA）。工会认可讲师对高等教育机构发展所作的贡献，但表示，非学术人员在机构有效运转所必需的行政、技术和运营活动中也发挥着关键作用。工会认为，未能给予非学术人员同等考虑，可能削弱机构效率并破坏和谐的劳资关系。声明补充称，长期拖延解决这些诉求，已在工会成员中引发广泛不满，并对相关机构的员工士气造成负面影响。工会敦促州政府利用这14天的最后通牒期，采取切实措施推动问题解决，并警告称，如果未能截至11月11日满足诉求，其领导层将依据劳动法于11月12日重新开会确定下一步行动。工会呼吁州长迈·马拉·布尼及其他相关政府利益相关方介入并解决这些诉求，以避免工业动荡以及该州高等教育机构教学和行政活动可能受到中断。加入 Daily Trust WhatsApp 社区，快速获取身边的新闻与动态

https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.title: FG moves to strengthen digital health data management
https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.summary: The federal government is stepping up efforts to improve health data management by strengthening the digital skills of health information professionals and ensuring that qualified officers are responsible for managing records in health care facilities.
https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.summary_zh: 联邦政府正加大力度改善卫生数据管理，通过加强卫生信息专业人员的数字技能，并确保由具备资质的官员负责管理医疗机构的记录。
https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.body: The federal government is stepping up efforts to improve health data management by strengthening the digital skills of health information professionals and ensuring that qualified officers are responsible for managing records in health care facilities. The Registrar and Chief Executive Officer of the Records Officers Registration Council of Nigeria, Alhaji Babagana Mustapha, said this was necessary to prepare health information management graduates for the increasing use of digital technology in Nigeria’s health care system. Mustapha spoke in Abuja at a two-day retreat and training on the District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) for tutors across health information management training institutions. He said the training was designed to improve tutors’ practical knowledge of digital health systems and ensure that students acquired the skills required for effective health data collection, analysis, reporting and utilisation. The registrar urged heads of departments and coordinators to ensure that the knowledge gained during the exercise was shared with other tutors and integrated into teaching activities. He also called for improved digital learning facilities, continuous professional development and adherence to data confidentiality, information security and professional ethics. Representing the Director of Planning, Research and Statistics at the Federal Ministry of Health, Dr Anthony Adoge said the government would continue to support efforts to position licensed Health Information Management (HIM) officers at the centre of health care data management. Adoge urged the council to recommend that all public and private health facilities employ licensed health records officers to manage their records departments, regardless of whether they had adopted digital systems. He also pledged that only licensed HIM officers would be engaged as enumerators during the mini Demographic and Health Survey scheduled for 2027. According to him, the ministry had deployed laptops to 6,000 primary health care centres on the condition that states provide evidence that licensed HIM officers were managing health data in the facilities. He said more than 5,000 primary health care centres had been digitalised within six months, while about 11,000 of Nigeria’s 37,000 health facilities were using electronic medical record systems. Adoge said the government wanted health information professionals to develop competencies that could meet international standards and enable them to interpret data for effective health care planning and decision-making. He warned professionals against surrendering their responsibilities to technology vendors, stressing that qualified health information officers must remain central to the management and interpretation of patients’ data. Also speaking, Dr Chizora Opara of the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, said reliable data was critical to achieving Nigeria’s target of ending open defecation by 2030. Opara said the National Clean Nigeria: Use the Toilet Campaign, launched in 2019, had recorded 184 local government areas as open-defecation-free. https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.title_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府着手加强数字健康数据管理
https://dailytrust.com/fg-moves-to-stren.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府正加大力度改善健康数据管理，通过提升卫生信息专业人员的数字技能，并确保由具备资格的人员负责管理医疗机构的记录。尼日利亚记录员注册委员会登记员兼首席执行官Alhaji Babagana Mustapha表示，此举对于培养卫生信息管理专业毕业生、使其适应尼日利亚医疗体系日益广泛使用的数字技术至关重要。Mustapha在阿布贾举行的为期两天的地区卫生信息软件2（DHIS2）进修与培训会议上发表上述讲话。此次培训面向卫生信息管理培训机构的导师。Mustapha表示，培训旨在提升导师对数字卫生系统的实践知识，并确保学生掌握有效收集、分析、报告和利用健康数据所需的技能。登记员敦促各部门负责人和协调员确保将此次培训获得的知识与其他导师分享，并纳入教学活动。他还呼吁改善数字学习设施、推动持续职业发展，并遵守数据保密、信息安全和职业伦理。联邦卫生部规划、研究与统计主任代表Dr Anthony Adoge表示，政府将继续支持相关工作，使持牌卫生信息管理（HIM）官员成为医疗数据管理的核心力量。Adoge敦促委员会建议所有公立和私立医疗机构，无论是否采用数字系统，均应聘用持牌健康记录员管理其记录部门。他还承诺，在定于2027年举行的微型人口与健康调查期间，只会聘用持牌HIM官员担任调查员。Adoge表示，卫生部已向6,000家初级卫生保健中心配发笔记本电脑，条件是各州须提供证据，证明这些设施由持牌HIM官员管理健康数据。他说，已有5,000多家初级卫生保健中心在六个月内完成数字化，尼日利亚37,000家医疗机构中约有11,000家正在使用电子病历系统。Adoge表示，政府希望卫生信息专业人员培养能够达到国际标准的能力，从而解读数据，为有效的医疗规划和决策提供支持。他警告专业人员不得将自身职责外包给技术供应商，强调合格卫生信息官员必须继续在患者数据的管理和解读中发挥核心作用。联邦水资源与卫生部Dr Chizora Opara也出席并发表讲话。他表示，可靠的数据对于实现尼日利亚到2030年消除露天排便的目标至关重要。Opara表示，2019年启动的“清洁尼日利亚：使用厕所”运动已使184个地方政府辖区实现无露天排便。加入《Daily Trust》WhatsApp社区，快速获取身边的新闻与动态

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.title: Can Tinubu’s education reforms rescue a generation? – Inside Alausa’s ambitious agenda
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.summary: With nearly 46 million children reportedly captured in a new education data system, almost 250,000 Nigerians undergoing technical skills training and the government claiming to have returned one million out-of-school children to classrooms, the Tinubu administration is making an ambitious case for an education turnaround. That is the central question confronting Alausa as he presents President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms as the beginning of a measurable turnaround.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.summary_zh: 据报道，近4600万名儿童已被纳入新的教育数据系统，尼日利亚近25万人正在接受技术技能培训，政府还宣称已让100万名失学儿童重返课堂。提努布政府正雄心勃勃地论证，扭转教育困境大有希望。这是阿拉乌萨面临的核心问题：他正在把总统博拉·提努布的教育改革描绘为一场成效可衡量的转型的开端。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.body: With nearly 46 million children reportedly captured in a new education data system, almost 250,000 Nigerians undergoing technical skills training and the government claiming to have returned one million out-of-school children to classrooms, the Tinubu administration is making an ambitious case for an education turnaround. But can impressive figures translate into lasting educational transformation? Now, in the office of the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, a digital dashboard is offering a different picture–one the minister says provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor schools, track enrolment, identify infrastructure gaps and examine the distribution of teachers and pupils nationwide. With a few clicks, Alausa explained, officials can drill down into individual schools to examine enrollment figures, the number of girls, available facilities and teaching personnel. For a country long challenged by fragmented education statistics, this represents a potentially significant shift. But the real test of Nigeria’s education reforms is not how impressive the dashboard appears in Abuja. It is whether the technology delivers better classrooms, competent teachers, improved learning outcomes and greater opportunities for millions of children. That is the central question confronting Alausa as he presents President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms as the beginning of a measurable turnaround. Together, these priorities seek to address a fundamental contradiction in Nigerian education: expanding access without guaranteeing learning, producing graduates without adequate practical skills and increasing enrolment without providing sufficient infrastructure. With Nigeria’s population estimated at approximately 220 million and a youthful demographic, Alausa argued that education reform was imperative. The challenge is to turn this demographic advantage into economic productivity rather than allow it to deepen unemployment, inequality and insecurity Perhaps the most consequential element of Alausa’s presentation was the ministry’s cloud-based education dashboard, which he said captures information on nearly 46 million children. Its potential lies in replacing fragmented administrative records with a more comprehensive picture of the education system. Reliable information could help authorities identify schools without adequate classrooms, locate teacher shortages, track enrolment and attendance, and direct resources towards underserved communities. For years, inadequate or inconsistent data have complicated education planning. Children who drop out may disappear from official records, while schools with urgent needs may struggle to attract appropriate interventions. A functioning digital system could change that by helping policymakers identify problems early and monitor whether government investments produce results.But there is a crucial distinction between collecting data and using it effectively. The minister’s presentation did not independently establish the completeness of the dashboard’s coverage, the frequency of updates or the extent to which its information has been verified against school-level records. For the system to become a credible accountability instrument, its data must be regularly updated, independently validated and linked to decisions on funding and intervention. Appropriate information should also be accessible to researchers, journalists and the public, without compromising children’s privacy. Otherwise, the dashboard risks becoming an expensive digital catalogue of problems rather than an instrument for solving them. Among the most compelling claims in Alausa’s presentation was that the government had brought approximately one million children back into school over the preceding three years. If independently verified and sustained, the achievement would represent a significant step towards addressing Nigeria’s persistent out-of-school crisis.Yet, educational exclusion is not simply a question of school admission. Poverty, insecurity, displacement, child labour, early marriage, inadequate infrastructure and the cost of schooling all contribute to keeping children away from classrooms. In conflict-affected communities, children may be enrolled but unable to attend safely. In poor households, the immediate need for income can outweigh the perceived benefits of education. Girls may face additional barriers, including household responsibilities, early marriage and inadequate sanitation facilities. Consequently, returning a child to school is only the beginning. The government must establish how many of the reported one million children remain enrolled, attend consistently, progress through school and acquire foundational literacy and numeracy skills. It must also demonstrate that interventions are reaching the hardest-to-reach populations, particularly children in remote rural settlements, economically disadvantaged households and communities affected by insecurity. Without transparent definitions, a clear baseline and independently verifiable evidence, the reported figure cannot by itself establish the extent to which Nigeria’s out-of-school crisis has been reduced. The country needs not merely children counted in school records, but children who attend, learn and complete their education. Another major pillar of Alausa’s agenda is technical and vocational education and training, under which he reported that nearly 250,000 Nigerians were undergoing skills training. The initiative challenges the longstanding perception that conventional university education is the principal route to success. Nigeria needs electricians, welders, mechanics, construction technicians, renewable-energy installers and manufacturing specialists whose expertise requires practical training rather than classroom theory alone.However, the number of people enrolled in training programmes is only an initial measure of success. The decisive questions concern the quality of instruction, relevance of the courses, availability of modern equipment and whether participants obtain recognised qualifications. More importantly, are trainees securing jobs, establishing businesses and earning sustainable incomes? Training institutions must work closely with employers to identify skills shortages, update curricula and provide practical experience. The government should publish completion rates, certification figures and employment outcomes to establish whether the initiative is creating genuine pathways to economic mobility. Without such evidence, Nigeria risks producing another generation of certificate holders without the practical competencies employers need. Alausa also identified girls’ education as a priority, citing approximately six million girls reached through interventions and referring to an initiative involving an African Development Bank credit facility of about $1.2 billion. The precise programme scope, financing terms and beneficiary figures require further clarification. Nevertheless, the policy direction addresses an important national challenge. Denying girls education restricts their employment opportunities, weakens their economic independence and deprives communities of the broader benefits associated with female education. The quality of teachers and education may ultimately determine whether the other reforms deliver lasting results.A country can build classrooms, enrol millions of pupils and introduce new curricula but still fail if children cannot read proficiently, understand mathematics or apply scientific knowledge. Teachers are the most immediate link between government policy and the child’s classroom experience. Strengthening science, technology, engineering, mathematics and medical sciences education therefore requires more than curriculum changes. It demands qualified teachers, functional laboratories, appropriate learning materials and effective practical instruction. Alausa also highlighted the shift towards competency-based and outcome-oriented curricula, an important response to a world increasingly shaped by technology, artificial intelligence and changing labour-market demands. But teachers need adequate preparation, continuous professional development and the resources to deliver these changes. Schools must also be assessed against credible learning benchmarks rather than judged mainly by enrolment, examination participation or certificates awarded. Without reliable evidence of improvements in reading, mathematics and science, it will remain difficult to determine whether the reforms are improving learning or merely expanding the machinery through which education is delivered. At the tertiary level, Alausa said the number of Nigerian universities appearing among the world’s top 1,000 to 1,200 institutions had increased from approximately 14 before Tinubu assumed office to 29. He also reported that the administration had invested more than ₦800 billion in student hostel construction across nearly 120 federal institutions over three years. If substantiated, these interventions point to efforts to improve institutional visibility and student welfare. Additional accommodation could ease overcrowding, improve safety and reduce the difficulties students face in securing housing. However, the value of the reported investment depends on how many hostels have been completed, how many bed spaces have become available and whether accommodation remains affordable. Similarly, international rankings provide useful indicators of research activity, reputation and institutional performance, but do not capture every dimension of educational quality. Research output, laboratory capacity, graduate employability, completion rates and teaching standards must also feature in assessments of university progress. Alausa also highlighted relative stability in the tertiary academic calendar. Reducing strikes and disruptions is essential to limiting delays, additional household expenses and declining confidence in the university system. But stability must be accompanied by adequate funding, improved working conditions, research facilities and better learning environments. The objective is not merely to keep universities open, but to make them productive centres of teaching, research and innovation. The controversy surrounding the management and funding of federal unity schools, including King’s College, Lagos, raises difficult questions about school financing, deteriorating infrastructure and the financial burden on parents.The government is right to recognise that public schools cannot consistently deliver quality education without adequate funding for facilities, teaching materials and essential services. However, reform cannot rest on the assumption that higher fees are justified simply because improvements are promised. Any adjustment must be supported by transparent costs, a clear account of how additional revenue will be spent and safeguards for pupils whose families cannot afford higher charges. Where government subsidies are intended, their terms should be publicly explained. The challenge is to develop a sustainable financing model that improves quality without excluding children from disadvantaged backgrounds. A reform that upgrades facilities but prices poorer pupils out of school would solve one problem by creating another. Alausa’s presentation offers an ambitious picture of an education system undergoing reform. The digital dashboard, reported return of one million children to school, expansion of technical training, girls’ education interventions, hostel investments and improved university rankings point to efforts to address longstanding weaknesses. It also needs independently verifiable data, transparent financing and accountability when programmes fail to achieve their objectives. Here lies the potential importance of Alausa’s dashboard.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.title_zh: 蒂努布的教育改革能否挽救一代人？——走进阿劳萨的雄心勃勃的议程
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/can-.body_zh:
据报道，一个新的教育数据系统已收录近4600万名儿童，尼日利亚近25万人正在接受技术技能培训，政府还宣称已让100万名失学儿童重返教室。廷努布政府正以雄心勃勃的举措推动教育扭转。但这些亮眼数字能否转化为持久的教育变革？如今，在教育部长 Tunji Alausa 博士的办公室里，一块数字仪表板呈现出另一番图景——部长称，这为监测学校、跟踪入学情况、查明基础设施缺口以及考察全国教师与学生分布提供了前所未有的机会。Alausa 解释道，只需点击几下，工作人员便可以深入查看个别学校，考察入学人数、女生人数、现有设施和教学人员。对于一个长期受统计数据碎片化困扰的国家而言，这可能代表着一项重大转变。但尼日利亚教育改革的真正考验，不是仪表板在阿布贾看起来多么漂亮，而是这项技术能否带来更好的课堂、称职的教师、 improved learning outcomes，以及为数百万儿童创造更多机会。这正是 Alausa 面对的核心问题；他将总统 Bola Tinubu 的教育改 presents 为一场可量化扭转的开端。这些优先事项共同试图解决尼日利亚教育中的一个根本矛盾：扩大入学机会却不能保障学习成果，培养毕业生却不具备足够的实践技能，提高入学率却没有提供充足的基础设施。鉴于尼日利亚人口估计约为2.2亿，且人口结构年轻，Alausa 认为教育改革势在必行。挑战在于把这一人口优势转化为经济生产力，而不是让它进一步加剧失业、不平等和不安全。Alausa 介绍中可能最具影响的一项内容，是教育部基于云端的教��仪表板；他称，该系统收录了近4600万名儿童的信息。其潜力在于用更完整的教育系统图景取代分散的行政记录。可靠信息可以帮助主管部门找出缺乏足够教室的学校，确定教师短缺的位置，追踪入学和出勤情况，并将资源投向服务不足的社区。多年来，数据不足或不一致使教育规划十分棘手。辍学儿童可能从官方记录中消失，而需求迫切的学校可能难以获得适当干预。一个运转良好的数字系统可以帮助决策者尽早发现问题，并监测政府投资是否产生成果。

但收集数据与有效利用数据之间有着关键区别。部长的介绍并未独立证明仪表板覆盖范围的完整性、更新频率，也未证明其中信息已与校级记录核验到什么程度。要让该系统成为可信的问责工具，其数据必须定期更新、接受独立验证，并与资金拨付和干预决策相衔接。相关信息也应向研究人员、记者和公众开放，同时不损害儿童的隐私。否则，这块仪表板可能沦为一份昂贵的数字问题目录，而不是解决问题的工具。

Alausa 介绍中最有说服力的说法之一，是政府在此前三年里已让约100万名儿童重返学校。若经独立核验并持续推进，这一成果将是应对尼日利亚长期失学危机的重大一步。

然而，教育排斥不单纯是学校录取问题。贫困、不安全、流离失所、童工、早婚、基础设施不足和教育成本，都会让儿童远离课堂。在受冲突影响的社区，儿童可能已经注册入学，却无法安全到校。在贫困家庭中，眼前的收入需求可能压过人们所认为的教育收益。女生还可能面临额外障碍，包括家庭责任、早婚和卫生设施不足。因此，让孩子重返学校只是开始。政府必须明确，在所报告的100万名儿童中，有多少人仍在校就读、持续出勤、顺利升学并掌握基础读写和计算技能。政府还必须证明，相关干预措施确实惠及最难触达的人群，尤其是偏远农村聚落、经济处境不利家庭以及受不安全局势影响的社区。如果没有透明的定义、明确的基线和独立可核验的证据，仅凭所报告的数字，无法判断尼日利亚的失学危机究竟在多大程度上得到缓解。这个国家需要的不只是被记入学校档案的儿童，而是能够出勤、学习并完成学业的儿童。

Alausa 议程的另一大支柱是技术与职业教育培训；他报告称，近25万名尼日利亚人正在接受技能培训。该举措挑战了长期以来“传统大学教育是成功主要道路”的观念。尼日利亚需要电工、焊工、机械师、建筑技术员、可再生能源安装人员和制造领域的专业人员，而他们的专长需要实践训练，而非仅靠课堂理论。

然而，参加培训项目的人数只是衡量成功的初步指标。决定性的问题在于教学质量、课程相关性、现代化设备的可用性，以及参与者能否获得受认可的职业资格。更重要的是，学员能否找到工作、创办企业并获得可持续收入？培训机构必须与雇主密切合作，找出技能短缺、更新课程并提供实践经验。政府应公布完成率、认证人数和就业结果，以证明该举措正在为经济流动创造真正可行的道路。如果没有这些证据，尼日利亚可能再培养出一代只有证书、却缺乏雇主所需实践能力的人。

Alausa 还把女生教育列为优先事项，称相关干预措施已惠及约600万名女生，并提到一项涉及 African Development Bank 约12亿美元信贷额度的计划。该计划的具体范围、融资条款和受益人数仍需进一步澄清。尽管如此，这一政策方向回应了一项重要的国家挑战。剥夺女生的受教育机会，会限制其就业前景，削弱其经济独立性，也会使社区无法享受女性教育带来的更广泛益处。师资和教育的质量，最终可能决定其他改革能否取得持久成果。

一个国家可以修建教室、招收数百万名学生、引入新课程，但如果儿童不能熟练阅读、理解数学或运用科学知识，仍然可能失败。教师是政府政策与儿童课堂体验之间最直接的纽带。因此，加强科学、技术、工程、数学和医学教育，不仅需要改变课程。它还需要合格教师、可正常使用的实验室、适当的学习材料和有效的实践教学。Alausa 还强调，课程正转向以胜任力和结果为导向，这是对 increasingly shaped by technology, artificial intelligence and changing labour-market demands 的世界作出的重要回应。但教师需要充分准备、持续专业发展以及实施这些变革所需的资源。学校的评估也必须以可信的学习基准为依据，而不能主要依据入学人数、考试参与度或颁发证书来评判。如果没有阅读、数学和科学进步的可靠证据，就很难判断这些改革究竟是在改善学习，还是仅仅在扩大教育供给体系。

在高等教育层面，Alausa 表示，跻身全球前1000至1200所大学之列的尼日利亚大学，已从廷努布就任前的约14所增加到29所。他还报告称，该政府在三年内投资超过₦800亿，在近120所联邦院校建设学生宿舍。若能证实，这些举措表明政府正努力提升院校知名度和学生福利。新增住宿空间可以缓解拥挤、改善安全状况，并减少学生寻找住房时面临的困难。然而，所报告投资的价值取决于有多少宿舍已经建成、有多少床位投入使用，以及住宿费用是否仍能被学生承受。同样，国际排名是衡量研究活跃度、声誉和院校表现的有用指标，但无法涵盖教育质量的每个维度。研究产出、实验室能力、毕业生就业率、完成率和教学标准，也必须纳入对大学进步的评估中。Alausa 还强调，高等教育校历相对稳定。减少罢课和中断，对于限制延期、减轻家庭额外支出以及维持人们对大学体系的信心至关重要。但稳定必须伴随充足资金、较好的工作条件、研究设施和更佳的学习环境。目标不只是让大学持续开门办学，而是要把大学建设成富有成效的教学、研究和创新中心。围绕联邦统一学校（包括 King’s College, Lagos）管理和资金问题的争议，对学校融资、基础设施恶化和家长经济负担提出了棘手问题。

政府认识到，如果不为设施、教学材料和基本服务提供充足资金，公立学校就无法持续提供优质教育，这是正确的。然而，改革不能建立在一种假设之上：仅仅因为承诺改善，就认定提高收费是合理的。任何调整都必须有透明的成本依据、清晰的额外收入使用说明，并为无力承担更高费用的学生家庭提供保障。若政府计划提供补贴，也应公开说明相关条款。挑战在于建立一种可持续的融资模式，在提升质量的同时不把出身弱势背景的儿童排除在外。一项改善了设施、却把贫困学生挤回校外的改革，无异于解决一个问题的同时制造另一个问题。

Alausa 的介绍展现了一幅雄心勃勃的教育改革图景。数字仪表板、让100万名儿童重返学校的报告、技术培训扩张、女生教育干预、宿舍投资以及大学排名提升，均指向解决长期积弊的努力。与此同时，它也需要独立可核验的数据、透明的融资机制，以及在项目未能实现目标时落实问责。这正是 Alausa 的仪表板可能具有重要价值之处。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/ndc-cannot-p.body: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of adopting double standards on accountability, insisting that the party must accept the same scrutiny it demanded of the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration. He said criticism of government decisions was a legitimate part of democratic governance and should not be dismissed as political hostility simply because the NDC was now in power. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 30, the Effutu MP questioned what he described as the party’s changing attitude towards public scrutiny after spending eight years in opposition challenging the policies, appointments, contracts and expenditure of the Akufo-Addo administration. “The NDC spent eight years teaching Ghanaians that questioning government was patriotism. Today, the same people appear offended that Ghanaians have taken those lessons seriously,” he wrote. Mr Afenyo-Markin argued that the NDC had previously maintained that no government should be above scrutiny and that public officials must account for their decisions. He questioned whether the party’s return to government had changed its position on those principles. “So what has changed? Have the standards of accountability changed because the political party in power has changed? Or was scrutiny only acceptable when it was directed at the NPP?” he asked. The Minority Leader accused some members of the governing party of responding to criticism by questioning the motives of those raising concerns, rather than addressing the issues themselves. He said the NDC’s past public statements, interviews and press conferences remained available for Ghanaians to assess its position on accountability while in opposition. “It is unreasonable to champion accountability for eight years and then treat it as an act of hostility when the same principle is applied to you,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin maintained that questioning government contracts, demanding transparency and assessing public expenditure were not personal attacks on public officials but essential elements of democratic oversight. “Public office is not a personal possession; it is a public trust. Holding office does not grant anyone immunity from criticism. Questioning a contract is not a personal attack on the person who approved it. Demanding transparency is not an expression of hatred. Asking government to honour its promises is not an attempt to undermine it. It is simply democracy at work,” he stated. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Minority would continue examining government documents, scrutinising contracts and questioning public spending, regardless of which political party was in power. He said the opposition’s role was not simply to oppose the government but to ensure that public officials were held accountable for their decisions and that government promises were measured against actual performance. “The Mighty Minority will continue to read the documents, examine the contracts, question public expenditure, and measure government promises against actual performance. Not because we are opposing the NDC for opposing sake, but because accountability must never depend on who occupies the Presidency,” he wrote. He further insisted that the NDC could not apply one standard to the NPP while in opposition and expect a different one now that it controlled the government. “If members of the NDC were right to demand accountability from the Akufo-Addo government, then they must be prepared to accept it now that they are in office,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin ended his post by pledging that the Minority would maintain its scrutiny of the government, arguing that the standards the NDC demanded while in opposition should equally apply to it in office. “The standard members of the NDC demanded when they were in opposition should be the same standard they must live by, and we, the Mighty Minority, will not renege!!” he added
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ndc-cannot-p.title_zh: NDC不能一面鼓吹问责，一面抵制监督
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ndc-cannot-p.body_zh: 少数派领袖亚历山大·阿费尼奥-马金指控执政的全国民主党（NDC）在问责问题上采取双重标准，坚持该党必须接受其此前要求前新爱国党（NPP）政府接受的同等审查。他说，批评政府决定是民主治理的合法组成部分，不应仅仅因为NDC如今执政就被斥为政治敌意。在10月30日星期五发布的一则脸书帖子中，这位埃富图选区议员质疑了他所称的该党在公共审查方面态度的转变，因为该党在反对党位置上度过8年，一直挑战阿库福-阿多政府的政策、任命、合同和支出。他写道：“NDC用了8年时间教导加纳人，质疑政府就是爱国。今天，同样这些人似乎对加纳人认真汲取这些教训感到愤怒。”阿费尼奥-马金认为，NDC此前一直主张任何政府都不应凌驾于监督之上，公共官员必须为其决定作出解释和说明。他质疑该党重新执政后是否改变了对这些原则的立场。他问道：“那么，究竟改变了什么？是因为执政党变了，问责标准就随之改变了吗？还是说，只有当审查针对NPP时才可接受？”少数派领袖指控执政党某些成员在回应批评时，会质疑提出问题者的动机，而不是处理问题本身。他说，NDC过去发表的公开声明、接受的采访和举行的新闻招待会仍可供加纳人查证，以了解该党在反对党时期对问责问题的立场。他说：“倡导问责8年，然后在同样的原则适用于自己时，却将其视为敌对行为，这是不合理的。”阿费尼奥-马金坚持认为，质疑政府合同、要求透明并评估公共支出并非对公职人员的人身攻击，而是民主监督不可或缺的组成部分。他说：“公职不是个人财产，而是一种公共信托。担任公职并不赋予任何人免受批评的特权。质疑一份合同并不是对批准合同者的个人攻击。要求透明并不是仇恨的表现。要求政府履行承诺也不是企图破坏政府。这只是民主制度在运作。”阿费尼奥-马金表示，无论哪个政党执政，少数派都将继续审查政府文件、检查合同并质疑公共支出。他说，反对派的职责不只是反对政府，还要确保公职人员为其决定负责，并以实际表现衡量政府承诺。他写道：“强大的少数派将继续阅读文件、检查合同、质疑公共支出，并以实际表现衡量政府承诺。我们这样做不是因为为了反对而反对NDC，而是因为问责绝不能取决于谁担任总统职位。”他进一步坚持，NDC不能在处于反对党地位时用一套标准要求NPP，而在如今掌控政府后却期待采用另一套标准。他说：“如果NDC成员在阿库福-阿多政府执政期间要求其承担的问责是正确的，那么如今他们自己执政时，就必须准备接受这种问责。”阿费尼奥-马金在帖子最后承诺，少数派将继续对政府进行监督，并认为NDC在反对党时期所要求的标准，同样应适用于其执政时期。他补充道：“NDC成员在处于反对党地位时所要求的标准，应当成为他们执政时必须遵守的标准，而我们强大的少数派绝不会退缩！！”
